alignments.note: Explicit subject pronoun takes only its own English (rule 20).
Verbless clause: the construction-supplied copula joins the nominal predicate (rule 20), and the indefinite article belongs to the noun that licenses it (rule 15).
Article on the rectum; the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase at all (*a rose of Sharon*), so rule 29's last sentence applies.
Construct relation goes to the nomen rectum, headed on the name (rule 19).
Construct noun keeps its own word; supplied indefinite article is the noun's own (rule 15).
Arthrous rendering of the rectum: the article takes the *the* standing before its own word (rule 29).
Rectum takes the relational *of*, headed on the noun (rules 19, 24).

review_notes: Two nominal clauses, each with a construct chain; the copula of the first is placed on the predicate under rule 20 and the second clause writes none.
